jobs.title: Director Enterprise Technology Architecture
jobs.description:
Position Summary

McGill University is seeking a Director Enterprise Technology Architecture, reporting to the Senior Director, IT Governance & Strategic Planning (GSP) to lead the e nterprise technology architecture strategy and roadmap, leading enterprise-wide architecture integration, architecture principles, standards, business capabilities and governance processes while promoting innovation, business value realization, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth.

The Director of Enterprise Architecture will play a strategic role between business strategy and technology directions
guiding the organization over the long term, from broad enterprise visions to solution-level decisions.
This role serves as a trusted and strategic advisor to business and technology leaders, ensuring that technology investments and transformation initiatives, are delivered toward a coherent target sate. This role is part of a transformation context: redefining the architecture operating model to increase the autonomy of delivery teams and establish the standards to support the growth and changes.
Key Responsibilities

Strategic Enterprise Architecture

Influence enterprise technology portfolio and investment planning by assessing strategic alignment, architectural fit, enterprise reuse opportunities, dependencies, technical debt implications, and long-term sustainability of proposed investments.
Develop and evolve the organization's business and enterprise architecture strategy, ensuring alignment with the institution vision, strategic priorities, and operational objectives.
Translate institutional strategy into target-state architectures, strategic architecture priorities, and actionable transformation roadmaps.
Develop integrated business and technology roadmaps that guide organizational transformation, investment planning, and modernization priorities.
Advise senior leadership on technology investments, enterprise capabilities, architectural implications, and transformation opportunities.
Shape architecture direction for strategic domains such as AI, data, application modernization, platforms, integration, and emerging technologies.
Guide application and platform rationalization to reduce redundancy, complexity, technical debt, and operational costs.
Establish and evolve enterprise business capability and value-chain models to support strategic planning, investment prioritization, and transformation.
Define enterprise reference architectures and target-state architecture that provide strategic direction for technology capabilities, platforms, and solution design.
Communicate enterprise architecture direction, outcomes, and value to executive leadership and key stakeholders.

Business and Technology Alignment

Act as a strategic partner between business and technology leadership, ensuring technology priorities and architecture decisions support institutional objectives.
Engage business and technology leaders to understand strategic needs, emerging priorities, and transformation opportunities, and translate them into architecture requirements and priorities.
Facilitate cross-functional alignment on business capabilities, technology direction, dependencies, and architectural trade-offs.
Partner with business and technology stakeholders to align initiatives and investment priorities with enterprise roadmaps and target-state architecture.
Provide architecture guidance to programs and delivery teams, ensuring business intent is effectively translated into scalable and sustainable technology solutions.
Identify and resolve gaps or conflicts between business priorities, technology strategies, and enterprise architecture direction.

Governance and Leadership

Establish and lead enterprise-wide architecture governance to drive consistent adoption of standards, patterns, decision frameworks, reference architectures, to enable strategic technology direction across business and technology domains.
Chair the Architecture Review Boards and other governance forums, ensuring effective architectural decision-making and cross-functional alignment.
Ensure strategic initiatives, programs, and solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, target-state architectures, and approved technology direction.
Stay abreast of industry trends, emerging technologies, market developments, and architectural best practices to inform enterprise architecture direction and decision-making.
Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, delivery teams, and technology stakeholders to strengthen architecture influence and organizational alignment.
Foster a culture of collaboration, innovation, architectural discipline, and continuous improvement.
Lead, mentor, and develop architecture practitioners while strengthening enterprise architecture capabilities, practices, and competencies across the organization.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related discipline.
Master’s degree in business administration (MBA) or relevant post-graduate studies in business is considered an asset.
Knowledge of the standard market architecture frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, ArchiMate, BIZBOK or equivalent) are considered strong assets.

Experience

Minimum 15 years of experience in technology, business architecture, enterprise architecture, strategy, business transformation, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role with team-management responsibilities;
Extensive experience developing and implementing enterprise architecture frameworks, business capability models, operating models, and strategic technology roadmaps.
Advanced proficiency across enterprise, business, and solution architecture, with the ability to operate effectively at every level while maintaining a strategic perspective.
Experience applying architecture principles and governance to complex organizational challenges.
Strong understanding of business process management, organizational design, capability-based planning, and information management.
Experience working across multiple business functions and technology domains.
Proven ability to influence senior executives and facilitate decision-making among diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated experience evaluating emerging technologies, including AI, and translating their potential business value into actionable technology transformation recommendations.

jobs.title: Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)

Duration: 3 Months

Reports: Chief Financial Officer

Location: Downtown Toronto (Hybrid)

Our client a North American professional services organization with multiple locations is seeking an experienced financial planning & analysis professional to lead a small team through a critical budgeting process. This individual will play a key role in guiding the organization through a complex budgeting and forecasting cycle while bringing greater structure, discipline, and insight to the overall financial planning process.

This is a highly hands-on assignment requiring an individual who is comfortable working directly in the details, partnering closely with operational and finance stakeholders, and supporting a team through a demanding planning period. The successful candidate will be equally comfortable rolling up their sleeves in Excel while providing strategic recommendations on process improvement, automation, and future-state planning capabilities.

Key Mandate

The Interim Director will be responsible for stabilizing, coordinating, and enhancing the organization's budgeting and forecasting processes while identifying opportunities to simplify workflows, improve data quality, and introduce practical technology solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and manage the organization's annual budgeting and forecasting process.
Provide day-to-day leadership, coaching, and support to a team of four FP&A professionals.
Work directly with budget owners and operational leaders to develop, validate, and challenge assumptions.
Consolidate and analyze budget submissions, identifying risks, opportunities, and variances.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support decision-making.
Ensure budget timelines, milestones, and deliverables are achieved.
Perform detailed hands-on analysis and modelling within a largely Excel-based environment.
Improve the consistency, accuracy, and transparency of financial reporting and forecasting.
Identify process bottlenecks and inefficiencies within the current budgeting framework.
Recommend practical opportunities for automation, simplification, and technology enablement.
Partner with senior leadership to provide meaningful insights into financial performance and future outlook.
Support the development of a roadmap for a more scalable and sustainable FP&A function.

Desired Experience

10+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, and business planning experience.
Previous experience serving as an Interim Director, FP&A Director, Finance Director, or equivalent senior finance leadership role.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale budgeting and forecasting cycles in complex organizations.
Strong people leadership experience with the ability to motivate and develop teams during periods of change.
Advanced Excel modelling skills and experience working in less structured finance environments.
Proven ability to create structure and discipline in processes that have evolved organically over time.
Experience implementing reporting, planning, or performance management improvements.
Exposure to budgeting and forecasting technologies, FP&A platforms, Power BI, automation tools, or similar solutions is considered an asset.
Strong communication and stakeholder management capabilities.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is not a pure strategist nor a pure analyst. They are a pragmatic finance leader who can quickly earn credibility, work collaboratively with the existing team, and balance immediate execution with longer-term process improvements.

They bring experience navigating ambiguity, are comfortable operating in Excel-based planning environments, and have a track record of introducing practical innovations that improve efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making without overcomplicating processes.

Expected Outcomes After 90 Days

Successful completion of the budgeting and forecasting cycle.
Improved forecasting accuracy and reporting consistency.
Enhanced structure, accountability, and governance within the planning process.
Increased confidence among stakeholders in financial plans and assumptions.
Identification of practical automation and technology opportunities.
Clear recommendations for future-state FP&A processes and tools to support scalability and improved decision-making.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION

Athletica Sport Systems Inc. is a global leader in the design, manufacturing, and installation of dasher board and arena systems, and the Preferred Rink Equipment Supplier of the NHL® and AHL®. Guided by our philosophy of “Safety through Innovation,” we have completed more than 3,000 projects worldwide from our headquarters in Waterloo, Ontario and operations in Minneapolis, London, and Vancouver.

Athletica is seeking a Director of Information Technology to join our leadership team in Waterloo. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this role owns technology, systems, and data across Athletica and its operating entities, supporting daily operations, organic growth, and acquisitions. The successful candidate will build and lead a growing IT team, stay hands-on while it matures, and lead the clean-up and cloud migration of our Epicor ERP, the technology side of a move to a new facility within 18 months of hire, and completion of our Microsoft Dynamics CRM implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy and budget: Translate business strategy into a sequenced technology roadmap with the CFO and leadership team, and manage the IT operating and capital budget, licensing, and vendor contracts.
Team: Staff, structure, and develop the IT team to meet business needs, using skills assessments to set hiring and training priorities and to engage outside partners. Stay hands-on while the team matures.
Epicor improvement: Own Epicor Kinetic end to end. Lead the clean-up and improvement of the existing implementation, including workflows, customizations, reports, and data quality, and standardize setups across entities.
Epicor platform: Keep Epicor current and supported, and lead the planned move from on-premises to Epicor in the cloud.
Epicor expertise: Build and train the IT team toward deep Epicor expertise and act as the conduit to outside specialists, including Six S Partners, reviewing designs, testing deliverables, and approving releases.
Manufacturing modernization: Keep operations on efficient, effective tools. Work with Operations, Engineering, and Projects to implement Epicor capabilities and technology such as barcode scanning, shop floor data collection, and mobile tools, and support Finance, which owns costing, with reliable system data.
Security & controls: Maintain role-based security in Epicor and other core systems, enforce segregation of duties and change management, and support financial controls and audits. Build a practical cybersecurity program covering multifactor authentication, endpoint protection, backup and recovery testing, and incident response.
Microsoft 365 & infrastructure: Own the Microsoft 365 environment and set direction for infrastructure and security, including which workloads stay on-premises and which move to the cloud.
Facility transition: Plan and lead the technology side of the move to the new facility, including network, telephony, shop floor connectivity, and cutover planning that limits disruption to production, installs, and shipping. Lead the expected Microsoft tenant reorganization, and sequence it with the Epicor upgrade and cloud migration.
CRM: Own Microsoft Dynamics CRM. Complete the partial implementation with sales, service, and finance leaders, fix data quality, simplify workflows, and integrate with Epicor and Microsoft 365.
Projects & platforms: Determine what project management capability Epicor and Dynamics already provide before recommending new platforms, and replace ad hoc spreadsheets and email processes with system workflows the business adopts.
Data, reporting & AI: Establish data ownership and standards, and set the reporting approach, including Power BI dashboards for bookings, backlog, margin, labor, capacity, and installs. Lead AI tool use, with Claude as the primary tool and Microsoft Copilot in limited use, within the company AI usage policy, and deploy a few high-value analytics and AI use cases.
M&A integration: Own the systems workstream for acquisitions, from diligence through integration, using a repeatable playbook for data migration, access setup, and process standardization.
Executive partnership: Translate how work happens across the business into system configurations, lead rollouts with training and post-go-live support, and represent technology with the board, banks, investors, and senior leadership.
Other duties as required

POSITION REQUIREMENTS

Education & Certifications:
·      Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
·      Certifications such as PMP, ITIL, CISSP, Microsoft, or Epicor are an asset.

Knowledge, Experience, and/or Technical Skills:
·      10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years leading an IT team in a manufacturing environment (required).
·      Hands-on experience with Epicor or another full-featured manufacturing ERP, including upgrades and role-based security design (required). Entry-level accounting packages do not qualify.
·      Experience with Epicor Kinetic, including on-premises to cloud migration, is a strong asset.
·      Working knowledge of manufacturing and financial processes, from bills of materials and routings to inventory, work in process, and the general ledger (required).
·      Microsoft 365 administration experience, including a tenant reorganization or migration (required).
·      Working knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics CRM, Power BI, and SQL.
·      Knowledge of IT general controls and cybersecurity practices, with experience supporting financial audits.
·      Experience delivering major technology projects, such as an ERP upgrade or facility move, with limited disruption to operations.
·      Proven ability to lead and develop a junior team, hire for skill gaps, manage vendors, and explain technical matters to business leaders.
·      Experience with multi-entity environments, acquisition integration, and applying AI tools is an asset.

Work Environment, Hours & Travel:
·      This role is based on-site at our Waterloo, Ontario facility, with occasional remote work at the discretion of the Chief Financial Officer.
·      Occasional travel is required to support other business units (Minneapolis, MN; London, ON; Vancouver, BC).
·      Standard full-time office hours, Monday to Friday, with flexibility for after-hours work during upgrades, cutovers, the facility move, and urgent incidents.
·      Some time on the production floor should be expected.

Compensation & Benefits:
·      Annual salary range: $120,000 to $150,000 CAD, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
·      Full-time, permanent position with eligibility to participate in Athletica's benefits program.
·      Opportunity to lead technology modernization at a global market leader.
